text:
Opening keynote at Fintech Builders Summit this morning: Helena Voss-Marchetti, founder and CEO of Larchmont Systems, on fraud detection for community banks. She has spent 20 years in payments infrastructure, founded and sold a payments company, and sits on two bank boards.

What stuck with me:

1. Her claim: small banks lose more to fraud per account than large banks because they buy rules, not models. Larchmont's customers have under $5B in assets, and most have no data-science team.

2. Her answer is one shared model across 90 banks, trained on pooled, anonymised fraud labels. Small banks get a model without having to build a team.

3. She expects regulators to require explainable fraud decisions within two years.

Best line of the morning: "A rule you can't update by Friday is a rule the fraudsters already know."

My GTM takeaway: when your buyer has no data-science team, you're selling an outcome, not a toolkit.

#Fintech #FraudDetection #CommunityBanking #FintechBuildersSummit
